newsitem.title: FINLAND: Forestry jitters keep Helsinki from highs.
newsitem.headline: Forestry jitters keep Helsinki from highs.

text.p: Shares remained close to year-highs but ended a lively Wednesday session a shade lower as forestries slipped ahead of UPM's and Metsa-Serla's eight-month reports, brokers said.
The HEX ended off 0.8 percent at 2,222.17 with volume a sturdy 420 million markka, 22 percent of it in Nokia.
"It depends on the UPM data whether forestries continue to slide," one broker said. Shares in Europe's biggest forestry group UPM-Kymmene lost 1.20 markka at 92.90 in cautious trade.
Merita advanced to 14.00 markka -- its highest since July 1995 -- up 0.50 in brisk demand after buy recommendations, as its stock made up 14 percent of bourse volume.
The HEX set its calendar year-high of 2,226.6 on October 8.

Pharmaceuticals wholesaler Tamro gained 0.50 markka to 32.50 ahead of eight-month data due on Thursday with volume boosted by a 40 million markka in-house deal by Protos Stockbrokers. Protos declined comment, and Tamro said it did not know who traded.
Cargo shipping firm Finnlines rose 2.50 markka to 108.00, its highest close since November 1995, as analysts said its chance to up its BTL stake may justify a yet higher valuation.

Food and chemicals group Raisio returned to sharp gains, ending up 16.00 markka at 279.00 after solid dealings ahead of an update from the group on its cholesterol-reducing Benecol margarine on October 24.
